label: Mulching
title: Mulching
description: I provide mulching services across Newquay, Truro, St Austell, and the wider Cornwall area. A proper mulch application tidies up your beds, suppresses weeds, retains moisture, and protects plant roots through Cornwall's milder but wetter winters. I supply quality bark mulch or composted material at market rate and handle the full job from bed prep through to a clean, even finish.

included.label: What’s included
included.title: A tidy bed refresh with a clean finish
included.description: Mulching is one of the simplest upgrades you can make to a garden, but it only works well when the preparation is done properly first. I clear weeds, tidy the bed edges, and make sure the soil surface is in good condition before laying anything down. In Cornwall's mild, damp climate, skipping this step just means weeds push straight through the mulch within a few weeks. I take the time to do it right so the result actually lasts. Once the beds are prepped, I apply mulch to an even depth for a consistent, tidy finish that makes the whole border look intentional.

items.title: Bed prep & tidy
items.description: Before any mulch goes down, I clear existing debris, pull weeds, and tidy the bed surface. Cornwall's year-round growing season means there is usually something sprouting, so thorough prep is essential. A clean bed gives the mulch the best chance of doing its job properly.

items.title: Weeding before mulching
items.description: Weeding before mulching is not optional if you want results that last. I remove weeds by hand and clear root systems where possible, particularly persistent growers like bindweed and couch grass that thrive in Cornwall's damp conditions. This gives you a much longer period before anything pushes back through.

items.title: Neat edging for a crisp line
items.description: A crisp, defined edge between lawn and bed makes the mulch look deliberate and contained. I cut fresh edges with a half-moon edger so the border has a clean line. This small detail makes a surprisingly big difference to how polished the finished job looks.

items.title: Mulch application
items.description: I spread mulch to an even depth across the bed, typically 5 to 8 centimetres depending on the material and the condition of the soil underneath. I supply either bark mulch for a decorative finish or composted material where the soil needs conditioning. Both are charged at market rate and itemised clearly in your quote.

items.title: Season-aware advice
items.description: Timing matters with mulching. Late autumn and early spring are the best windows in Cornwall. Autumn mulching locks in warmth and moisture before winter, while spring application suppresses weed germination as temperatures rise. I will advise on the ideal timing for your garden based on what you are growing and where you are in the county.

items.title: Waste removal (optional)
items.description: Any waste from bed preparation, including old mulch, weeds, and debris, is cleared away and taken off-site. I am a licensed waste carrier, so disposal is handled properly and legally. Green waste removal is charged at £10 per dumpy bag.

results.label: Recent results
results.title: Beds that look sharper and stay cleaner
results.description: A good mulch application changes the entire character of a border. Beds go from patchy and weedy to clean, uniform, and tidy. It is one of those jobs where the visual difference is immediate and obvious, which is why I enjoy doing it. The beds below were all prepped, weeded, edged, and mulched as part of a single visit.

bullets.title: Supports healthier growth
bullets.description: Mulch insulates plant roots from temperature swings, retains moisture during dry periods, and gradually breaks down to improve soil structure. In Cornwall's variable coastal climate, this protection is particularly valuable through winter.

bullets.title: Practical improvement

faq.label: FAQs
faq.title: Quick answers
faq.description: If you don’t see your question here, just get in touch.

items.question: What does mulching include?
items.answer: Mulching includes full bed preparation, mulch supply, and application to an even finish. Before laying any mulch, I clear weeds, tidy borders, and make sure the soil surface is ready so the mulch does its job properly. The mulch itself is spread to an even depth across your beds, giving them a clean, tidy look while helping to suppress weeds, retain moisture, and protect plant roots. I supply the mulch at market rate and include bed prep and even application in the service, so you get a complete job rather than just material dumped in the garden.

items.question: When is the best time to mulch?
items.answer: Late autumn or early spring are the best times to mulch. Applying mulch in autumn protects roots over winter and locks in moisture before the colder months. Spring mulching helps suppress weeds as they start to germinate and gives beds a fresh, tidy appearance for the growing season ahead. In Cornwall, the milder winters mean autumn mulching is particularly effective because the soil stays warmer for longer, giving plants a head start. That said, mulching can be done at any time of year if beds need attention. I will advise on the best timing for your situation.

items.question: Do you remove waste?
items.answer: Yes. Any waste generated during bed preparation, such as old mulch, weeds, or debris, is cleared away and taken off-site. Green waste removal is charged at £10 per dumpy bag. I am a licensed waste carrier, so disposal is handled properly and legally. I will give you an idea of likely waste costs when quoting the job.

items.question: Do you supply the mulch?
items.answer: Yes, I supply the mulch and charge it at market rate. This means you do not need to worry about sourcing, transporting, or storing bags of material yourself. I use quality mulch suited to the job, whether that is bark mulch for ornamental beds or composted material for improving soil condition. If you have a preference for a particular type, I am happy to accommodate that. The cost of materials is always itemised clearly in your quote so you can see exactly what you are paying for.

items.question: Do you cover my area?
items.answer: I am based near Newquay and cover a good chunk of Cornwall, including Truro, St Austell, Bodmin, Padstow, Perranporth, and St Ives. If you are within that area, I can usually fit you in without any issue. If you are slightly further afield, feel free to get in touch anyway and I will let you know if I can help.
